Als VC-backed Foodtech-Startup schaffen wir den Spagat zwischen gesunder Ernährung, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit. Mit unseren Foodjis bringen wir ultrafrische, leckere Gerichte genau dorthin, wo du die meiste Zeit verbringst – denn wir haben uns zum Ziel gesetzt, über 10 Millionen Arbeitnehmern endlich Zugang zu gesunder Ernährung zu ermöglichen und gleichzeitig Foodwaste zu reduzieren.

Gestalte das perfekte Foodji-Erlebnis

Ein großartiges Produkt allein reicht nicht – echte Kundenzufriedenheit entsteht durch starke Beziehungen und einen klaren Blick auf die Entwicklung des Kundenportfolios. Du machst den konkreten Nutzen und Mehrwert von Foodji sichtbar und schaffst damit die Grundlage für langfristige Partnerschaften.

Deine Mission bei Foodji:

  • (Enterprise-) Kund:innen begleitest du von der Testphase über den Vertragsabschluss durch die gesamte Customer Lifetime.

  • Für dein Kundenportfolio übernimmst du Verantwortung und sorgst dafür, dass Kund:innen Foodji erfolgreich nutzen, langfristig bleiben, wachsen und uns weiterempfehlen.

  • Stabile und vertrauensvolle Beziehungen zu zentralen Entscheider:innen und dezentralen Stakeholdern baust du gezielt auf und entwickelst sie weiter.

  • Verantwortung für die Gesundheit und Weiterentwicklung deines Enterprise-Kundenportfolios – von der KPI-basierten Analyse der Account Health bis zur Ableitung gezielter Maßnahmen.

  • Vertragsverlängerungen bereitest du aktiv vor und erkennst Kündigungsrisiken frühzeitig – auch wenn sie zunächst nur an einem einzelnen Standort auftreten.

  • Steuerung von internen und crossfunktionalen Projekten zur Weiterentwicklung des Customer Success Bereichs.


DAS BRINGST DU MIT

  • Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im Customer Success Management sowie nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Steuerung von Retention-, Vertragsverlängerungs- und Churn-Kennzahlen über ein Kundenportfolio hinweg.

  • Strukturierte, datengetriebene und eigenständige Arbeitsweise mit einem guten Gespür für Kundenbeziehungen sowie der Fähigkeit, Risiken, Kundenpotenziale und nächste Schritte selbstständig zu priorisieren.

  • Erfahrung im Umgang mit CRM-Systemen, insbesondere Salesforce, sowie sehr gute Excel-Kenntnisse.

  • Kommunikationsstärke auf Entscheider:innenebene – auch in anspruchsvollen Gesprächen – sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe Multi-Standort-Accounts mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern strategisch zu betreuen.

  • Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie fließende Englischkenntnisse.

  • Präsentations- und Argumentationsfähigkeit sowie ausgeprägte Networking-Kompetenzen.

  • Ein „Do-it“-Mindset, Teamfähigkeit, Selbstbewusstsein sowie eine lösungs- und zielorientierte Arbeitsweise.

NOCH FRAGEN?

Wir freuen uns auf deine Nachricht und helfen dir gerne weiter!

DAS BIETEN WIR

  • Office Foodji & Lunchit App: Immer bestens versorgt bei uns im Office oder Remote

  • Uncapped Bonus: Deine Leistung bestimmt dein Gehalt – nach oben gibt es keine Grenze

  • bAV: Mit der Degura Pension Cloud sichern und bezuschussen wir jetzt schon deine Rente

  • Spendit Card: Wir stocken dein Gehalt auf! Mit Spendit stehen dir bis zu fünfzig Euro netto im Monat on top zur freien Verfügung

  • EGYM Wellpass: Mit uns bleibst du fit & wir bringen dich deutschlandweit in die angesagtesten Fitness- und Wellnessstudios

  • JobRad: Spring mit uns aufs Rad und lease dir dein Traumrad oder Pedelec

  • KITA/Kiga Kostenzuschuss: Wir bezuschussen deine Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung, damit deine Kinder immer bestens versorgt sind

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Du erhältst attraktive Promotions und Discounts verschiedener Brands

  • Food Tastings: Teste dich mit unserem Foodteam durch unsere Produkte und gestalte unser Sortiment von morgen

  • Development: Deine Weiterentwicklung liegt uns am Herzen und mit regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und Trainings bieten wir dir spannende Entwicklungspfade – z. B. vom SDR zum Account Executive

  • Flexwork: Arbeite 30 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU Ausland

  • Top Office Lage: Genieße eine erstklassige Arbeitsumgebung im Münchener Glockenbachviertel mit der Isar vor der Tür

  • Team Events: Wir sind ein Team - beim Skiday, Frühstück, Culture Week oder Office Party feiern wir gemeinsam!

ÜBER UNS

Hi, schön, dass du da bist! Wir sind Foodji - ein Team aus Food-Lovern & Tech-Nerds.

Unsere Mission ist es, frisches, gesundes und vor allem leckeres Essen überall dort anzubieten, wo Menschen den Großteil ihres Alltags verbringen – in Büros, ganz gleich, ob im Gewerbegebiet oder mitten in der Stadt, während langer Schichten im Krankenhaus oder in den Tiefen einer Produktionshalle, in der rund um die Uhr Menschen arbeiten. Überall bieten wir vollwertige Gerichte, Snacks und Getränke genau dort an, wo und wann du sie brauchst.

Proprietäre Technologien, selbstlernende Algorithmen und effiziente Lieferketten helfen uns dabei, das Paradox zwischen frischem Essen, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit aufzulösen. Mit unserer eigens entwickelten Technologieplattform optimieren wir die Mengenplanung und sagen Food Waste den Kampf an. Wir wollen einen positiven Effekt erzielen – auf die Umwelt, den Alltag unserer Kund:innen und unsere Communities. Deshalb spenden wir übrig gebliebene Gerichte an Foodsharing und andere soziale Initiativen direkt vor unserer Haustür.

Als Marktführer versorgen wir mit Foodji bereits täglich Tausende Menschen in ganz Deutschland. Zu unseren Kund:innen zählen unter anderem der Münchner Flughafen, Klarna, Enpal und Wingcopter. Und wir fangen gerade erst an: Allein in Deutschland gibt es mehr als 100.000 relevante Standorte für uns.

Trage auch du deinen Teil dazu bei und bewirb dich jetzt.

data.description:
Aufgaben 

Du willst Technologie gestalten, die direkt etwas bewegt? 

Bei Table.Briefings entwickeln wir digitale Produkte für ein wachsendes Medienunternehmen. Unsere Software hilft dabei, Prozesse effizienter zu machen, neue Geschäftsmodelle zu ermöglichen und unseren Redaktionen den Rücken freizuhalten – damit sie sich auf das konzentrieren können, was sie am besten können: hochwertigen Journalismus!
Als dritter interner Entwickler bzw. dritte interne Entwicklerin übernimmst du eine zentrale Rolle in unserem Tech-Team. Du arbeitest an der gesamten Entwicklungskette: von der ersten Idee über Konzeption und Umsetzung bis zu Deployment, Betrieb und Weiterentwicklung.
Dabei geht es nicht nur darum, Features zu programmieren. Du hilfst uns, die richtigen Probleme zu erkennen, Anforderungen zu schärfen und Lösungen zu entwickeln, die für unser Business, unsere Nutzerinnen und Nutzer und unsere Redaktionen wirklich einen Unterschied machen. 


Deine Aufgaben 

  • Du konzipierst, entwickelst und betreust unsere Webanwendungen, APIs und Apps.
  • Du arbeitest an unseren Statamic-basierten Plattformen und entwickelst unser CMS weiter.
  • Du entwickelst neue Funktionen mit unserem bestehenden Tech-Stack und verbesserst bestehende Lösungen kontinuierlich.
  • Du beschäftigst dich mit dem Einsatz und der Optimierung von Large Language Models und Coding Agents– zur Automatisierung interner Prozesse und für neue Produktfeatures.
  • Du entwickelst und integrierst RESTful APIs, zum Beispiel zur Anbindung von Systemen wie ActiveCampaign.
  • Du wirkst bei der Konfiguration, Wartung und Absicherung unserer Linux-Server und Deployment-Prozesse mit.
  • Du übersetzt Anforderungen aus unterschiedlichen Bereichen in klare technische Lösungen.
  • Du bringst Struktur in komplexe oder noch nicht vollständig definierte Aufgaben und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen umsetzbare Produkte werden.
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Stakeholdern, Produktverantwortlichen, Redaktion und Geschäftsführung zusammen.

Unser Tech-Stack - Wir arbeiten unter anderem mit: 

  • PHP und Laravel
  • Statamic
  • PostgreSQL
  • Livewire
  • HTML, CSS und JavaScript
  • RESTful APIs
  • Linux-Servern und modernen Deployment-Prozessen
  • Large Language Models und Coding Agents
Du musst unseren Tech-Stack nicht bereits vollständig beherrschen – wichtiger sind uns dein technisches Verständnis, deine Kommunikationsstärke und deine Fähigkeit, komplexe Anforderungen schnell in gute Lösungen zu übersetzen. Du solltest aber Lust haben, mit unseren Technologien zu arbeiten und dich schnell in neue Systeme und Themen einzuarbeiten. 
Wir suchen keine Person, die jedes Tool schon einmal eingesetzt hat, sondern jemanden, der gute technische Entscheidungen trifft, Zusammenhänge versteht und Verantwortung übernimmt.


Qualifikation

  • Du hast fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und beherrschst mindestens eine relevante Programmiersprache sicher.
  • Du hast idealerweise Erfahrung mit Webanwendungen, APIs und Datenbanken.
  • Du interessierst dich für unseren Tech-Stack und hast Lust, dich inLaravel,Statamic, PostgreSQL und Livewire einzuarbeiten oder darin weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Du verstehst, wie man LLMs und CodingAgentssinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll in der Softwareentwicklung einsetzt – oder möchtest es lernen.
  • Du kennst dich mit Linux-Servern,Deploymentund grundlegenden Fragen der IT-Sicherheit aus oder bist bereit, dich in diese Themen einzuarbeiten.
  • Du kannst komplexe Probleme schnell erfassen, priorisieren und in konkrete nächste Schritte übersetzen.
  • Du kommunizierst klar und gerne – auch mit Menschen, die nicht technisch arbeiten.
  • Du kannst unterschiedliche Anforderungen und Perspektiven zusammenbringen und sicher mit Stakeholdern umgehen.
  • Du arbeitest selbstständig, zuverlässig und lösungsorientiert.
  • Du behältst auch dann den Überblick, wenn Anforderungen sich verändern, Informationen zunächst unvollständig sind oder mehrere Themen gleichzeitig auf dem Tisch liegen.
  • Du hast Freude daran, in solchen Situationen Ruhe, Struktur und Verbindlichkeit zu schaffen.
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sind für die Kommunikation im Team und mit unseren Stakeholdern unerlässlich.

Was uns wichtig ist

Wir entwickeln nicht zum Selbstzweck. Unser Ziel ist Software, die unmittelbar Wirkung entfaltet: für unser Geschäft, für die Vervielfachung unserer Lizenzen und für unsere Redaktionen, die täglich anspruchsvolle Inhalte produzieren.
Dafür suchen wir eine Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Fragen stellt und sich aktiv einbringt. Du solltest dich in einem meinungsstarken, dynamischen Umfeld wohlfühlen, unterschiedliche Perspektiven aushalten und deine eigenen Ideen überzeugend vertreten können. Gleichzeitig ist uns wichtig, dass du pragmatisch bleibst und gemeinsam mit anderen zu guten Lösungen kommst.


Benefits

Wir bieten dir: 

  • Eine Schlüsselposition in einem innovativen und wachstumsstarken Medienunternehmen
  • Die Möglichkeit,unseren Tech-Stackaktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln
  • Viel Eigenverantwortung und kurze Entscheidungswege
  • Einen vielseitigen Job mit direktem Einfluss auf unser Business und unsere Produkte
  • Eine unbefristete Festanstellung in Teilzeit oder Vollzeit
  • 28 Tage Urlaub
  • Flexibilität bei Arbeitszeit und Arbeitsort > Drei Tage pro Woche in unserem Büro in Berlin-Mitte, zwei Tage im MobileOffice
  • Persönliche und fachliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einer echten Wachstumskultur
  • Eine offene, freundliche Atmosphäre mit Partnerinnen, Partnern und Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus der ganzen Welt


Deine Bewerbung 

Wir freuen uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und ein kurzes, persönliches Motivationsschreiben mit maximal 1.000 Zeichen: Warum möchtest du als Full Stack Product Developer (m/w/d) bei Table.Briefings arbeiten? 

Uns interessiert besonders, welche Probleme du gerne löst, wie du mit unterschiedlichen Anforderungen umgehst und was dich daran reizt, Technologie mit konkretem unternehmerischem und redaktionellem Nutzen zu entwickeln.

data.description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We are looking for a sales engineer to join our sales team and drive the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.

This role bridges the technical and commercial worlds. You'll need interpersonal and technical skills to build relationships with process engineers in cement plants and understand their challenges. Analytical skills will be essential to delve deep into complex plant data and work out how Gigaton's AI products can solve their most critical issues.

Building on that, you'll need strategic thinking and commercial awareness to turn your findings into concise, compelling proposals for decision-makers at our customers, from the C-suite down.

Ultimately, you'll build clarity from uncertainty, making sure we agree a shared roadmap with our customers that puts our solutions on track for significant real-world benefits before a contract is signed.

Over time, you’ll help us evolve our sales approach and shape the product by feeding insights and needs from the plant back to the product team, building the foundation for scaling across industries.

Your main responsibilities

  • Be the technical expert on sales calls and visits with cement plants.

  • Build trust with process engineers and plant teams by understanding their specific plant issues and linking them to how we can help.

  • Analyse plant data to identify and evaluate opportunities, then use this analysis to create compelling sales proposals.

  • Lead technical discovery and identify early when a plant does not meet our ICP (ideal customer profile) criteria.

  • Make sure relationships and plant understanding are handed over successfully to the deployment team.

  • Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that help shape our product roadmap.

  • Develop and iterate the pre-sales technical process, making it more impactful and more automated each time.

  • Travel to plants and conferences, around one week per month, to understand customer environments and explain the product.

What a great fit looks like

  • Exposure to physical sciences, controls, or heavy industry, such as cement, steel, energy, manufacturing, or similar.

  • Strong analytical skills and an outcome-oriented mindset. You can dig into industrial data, identify root causes, generate potential solutions, and explain their value in dollars and tonnes of CO2.

  • Excellent communication skills. You can build credibility and trust in complex industrial environments with both engineers and board-level stakeholders.

  • Comfortable being the technical voice in the conversation, presenting to senior plant leaders and operators, handling objections, and being challenged on your findings by people who have run kilns for 30 years.

  • Naturally curious and keen to learn about the industry, the technology, and each individual plant. You want to understand the root cause behind every question and objection so you can solve the right problem.

  • Confident in ambiguity and able to field very specific technical questions without getting flustered. You know when you can give your understanding, when you need to go and find the answer, and how to maintain customer confidence in both situations.

  • Willingness to travel regularly.

You’ll excel if

  • You build trust easily. You can connect with plant engineers, listen deeply, and align solutions to their priorities.

  • You’d rather diagnose than pitch. Your first instinct in a plant is to ask a better question, not to open the deck.

  • You thrive in dynamic environments. Fast-paced, ambiguous settings excite you, and you’re motivated by high-impact, mission-driven work.

  • You have experience working in heavy industry, particularly cement, steel, energy, heavy manufacturing, or similar.

Success in This Role Means

  • Plants say yes because the technical case is clear. You build customer confidence that Gigaton can deliver high ROI, helping us hit our revenue goals without losing deals because customers don’t understand or believe in our product and capabilities.

  • Deployments are set up to succeed. We haven’t overpromised to sign a contract, and our pre-contract analysis holds up once the system is live.

  • Process engineers trust and rely on you as a partner in solving problems.

  • Deals don’t stall waiting on a technical answer. Objections get handled quickly, and customers get the answers they need in good time.

    💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match.

    We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from all walks of life, with different countries, cultures, and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

    We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process

  1. Talent Partner Screen Call: Meet our talent partner and learn more about Gigaton and the role.

  2. Hiring Manager Screen: Meet our VP of Sales and discuss if this role is a good fit for you.

  3. Technical Onsite (completed on the same day):

    1. Technical interview

    2. Data analysis & presentation

  4. Operating Principles Interview: Understand how we work and whether Gigaton and you are a good fit for each other.

  5. Meet with the CEO: Every new potential hire meets Josh.

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty: Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership: High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun: Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $96 million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io. We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are

  • You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

  • You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

About Exa

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion.

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers Agents, Fortune 500s, and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're a team of ~100 from Harvard, MIT, Meta, Google Research, ex-founders, and dropouts alike. We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We're high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

 

About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers are the technical tip of the spear at Exa. Partnered with an Account Executive, you own the technical win: you run discovery with customer engineering teams, design solutions on Exa's API, build and deliver demos and POCs that prove value, and turn technical evaluations into closed deals. You'll be one of the first GTM engineers in your region — you'll help define how Exa sells there, not just execute a playbook.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical side of the sales cycle: discovery, solution design, demos, POCs/POVs, and technical objection handling, in partnership with your AE

  • Run the technical side of expansion: spot new use cases in existing accounts and turn them into evaluations, with your AE

  • Build working demos and prototypes on Exa's API tailored to each customer's use case — agents, research, search, enrichment

  • Tell the story: translate Exa's capabilities into use-case narratives that land with CTOs, engineers, and PMs alike

  • Be the trusted technical advisor: know Exa inside out — the product, the API, the problems it solves — answer hard questions honestly, run evaluations rigorously, and know when to pull in engineering

  • Feed the field back into product: identify patterns across customer evaluations and channel them to product and engineering

  • Scale yourself and the region: build reusable demos, integration patterns, and playbooks, and represent Exa at technical workshops, meetups, and conferences

  • As a founding regional hire, support early customers through onboarding and initial implementation while we build out dedicated post-sales

Requirements

  • 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role (flexible for exceptional candidates) — solutions/sales engineering, solutions architecture, or an engineering role with heavy customer exposure (e.g., engineering lead, developer relations, technical consulting)

  • Technical depth with APIs and modern development (e.g. Python or TypeScript): you can design an integration, build a working demo, and debug it live — using AI-assisted tooling is expected, hand-crafted code is not the bar

  • Strong communication and presentation skills: you can command a room, adapt to your audience, and say "I don't know — I'll find out" when you don't

  • Comfort with ambiguity and early-stage intensity: you can run several evaluations in parallel, prioritize what moves deals, and your job description will change as the region grows

  • Familiarity with the modern AI stack — LLMs, RAG, agents — and how customers evaluate it; you can scope a POC with clear success criteria

  • Based in region with willingness to travel for customer engagements

  • Have owned technical evaluations at a developer-platform / API-first company — POCs/POVs you scoped and ran that ended in a customer going live

  • Have led engineers and want to move toward the customer, or are an SE who wants to be more hands-on than your last role allowed

  • Are genuinely curious about AI and have built things with LLMs — side projects count

  • Are energized by being the first: first hire, first deal, first playbook in a region

  • Have run enterprise evaluations end-to-end — POC success criteria, security questionnaires, RFP responses

You'll lead preventative and corrective maintenance activities, develop and deliver maintenance plans, and use data and root cause analysis to reduce downtime and improve equipment reliability. You'll also coach and support colleagues, champion engineering standards and work closely with Production, Technical and Engineering teams to achieve shared goals.

We're looking for someone who combines strong technical expertise with excellent planning and leadership skills, and who thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

    Review line performance, analyse incidents and equipment stops, and implement solutions that improve reliability and reduce downtime

data.description:
What is the job?

We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst, Marketing Analytics to help us uncover what’s truly driving growth, understand where the biggest opportunities lie and shape where we focus next.

This is a high-impact, hands-on senior individual contributor role for someone who loves getting under the skin of the data, connecting the dots behind performance and turning complex findings into clear, commercially meaningful action. You’ll be equally excited by the technical side of analytics - working with data, tools and reporting infrastructure - as you are by solving real business problems and influencing decisions.

Working closely with teams across paid media, CRM and lifecycle marketing, you’ll become a trusted partner to the wider marketing function. You’ll help us understand how our channels and campaigns are performing, identify the behaviours and trends that matter, and provide the insight needed to make smarter decisions about investment, optimisation and growth.

This is much more than a reporting role. You’ll challenge assumptions, ask the questions others may not have considered and bring clarity to complex or ambiguous problems. You’ll help shape how we measure success, improve the quality and accessibility of our marketing data, and build a stronger understanding of the full customer journey.

We’re looking for someone who is naturally curious, commercially minded and confident working independently. You’ll be comfortable setting your own direction, prioritising the work that will create the greatest value and getting on with delivering meaningful, measurable impact.

What will you be doing?

  • Partner with marketing teams to provide clear, actionable insights on performance across channels including Google, Meta, Social and CRM.

  • Analyse marketing spend and outcomes to support optimisation and better decision-making.

  • Own and evolve our GA4 setup, ensuring tracking is robust and focused on meaningful performance metrics.

  • Work with CRM teams to analyse lifecycle journeys, retention, and engagement using a variety of data sources.

  • Act as the internal owner for marketing data requirements, working with Analytics Engineers to ensure data models and dashboards meet real business needs.

  • Lead the development of advanced measurement, beyond basic attribution, moving from LTV and CAC towards incrementality.

  • Communicate insights clearly through dashboards, presentations, and conversations with senior stakeholders.

What do you need?

  • Experience with digital analytics, ideally in a fast-paced or growth-focused environment.

  • Hands-on experience with SQL is a must, BigQuery, GA4, Looker, and Google Sheets are a plus. Comfortable working across a broad marketing function and building strong relationships with non-technical stakeholders.

  • Experience collaborating with data or analytics engineering teams, clearly defining requirements and translating insight into action.

  • A confident communicator who can explain complex analysis in simple, practical terms. You’re able to identify the what and the why to help shape decisions.

  • Self-starter mindset - able to navigate ambiguity and work independently.

  • Experience with Braze or similar CRM platforms is a strong advantage.

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + usual bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, private healthcare and more

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. data.description:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Open to hiring remote in London, UK.

 

You will carry a book of 40-60 mid-market and emerging accounts - companies in the <$1B range, closing 25-40 deals a year at $40k-$100k and building toward larger standard deal sizes as our packaging moves upmarket. You work in a pod with a dedicated Mid-Market Engagement Manager on a shared book, with a comp plan designed to maximize earnings and customer value.

 

We are architecting the best GTM team in all of AI. If you want to grow, run fast, and sell with a leading-edge frontier AI company with room to grow your career, please apply.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Run a high-velocity full-cycle motion: 25-40 closed deals a year across inbound and outbound

  • Qualify hard and fast - your book is big, your calendar is the scarce resource, orientation to clear ROI and value orientation is a must

  • Push deal size up: committed-volume, use-case expansion plays that turn $30k starts into $100k+ repeatable motions

  • Turn product signals (usage spikes, team signups, credit burn) into pipeline

  • Work with your pod's Engagement Manager so new customers hit consumption targets and your held-back commission unlocks

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 3+ years of full-cycle closing experience in SaaS/AI with a quota record above 100%

  • Velocity evidence: 20+ closed deals a year, multi-channel prospecting, disciplined qualification

  • Native AI-tool fluency - you already sell with AI in your workflow, not despite it

  • Writing and demo skills strong enough to carry a deal without a solutions engineer

The Company:

When it comes to digital communities, The Alliance is leading the way. Product marketing, sales enablement, product-led growth, AI, customer success, CMOs, you name it, we’re home to thriving communities for them all.

With 160,000+ professionals across our communities and a constant stream of events, memberships, and learning products, we help individuals and teams grow faster in their careers. We work with some of the world’s most recognisable companies and pride ourselves on being a high-impact learning partner, not just another events business.

We’re ambitious, we move quickly, and we’re still early in the journey. That means real ownership, a steep learning curve, and plenty of opportunity to shape what comes next.

About the Role

We’re hiring early-career Sales Associates to join our Delegate & Membership sales team, people with energy, curiosity, and the drive to build a career in commercial roles.

This is a junior role by design. You don’t need years of experience, what matters most is how quickly you learn, how well you take feedback, and how comfortable you are being challenged. We’ll teach you how to sell properly: how to prospect, qualify, handle objections, manage a pipeline, and close, all while speaking to senior decision-makers at some of the world’s biggest tech companies.

You’ll sell across our live events, memberships, and learning solutions in markets including London, New York, San Francisco, Las Vegas and beyond. Over time, this role can progress into more senior sales or specialist commercial paths across the business.

This role is not about arriving fully formed, it’s about building and proving confidence, capability, and momentum through doing.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Sales Upskilling: You’ll build strong foundations in prospecting, qualification, pipeline management, and closing, while learning how to sell confidently to senior B2B stakeholders and work to clear targets and expectations.

  • Engaging decision-makers: You’ll speak directly with professionals at fast-growing and enterprise tech companies, understand their challenges, and recommend the right events, memberships, and learning solutions.

  • Owning deals end-to-end: You’ll own your pipeline from first contact through to close and handover, taking accountability for outcomes and using feedback and data to improve week by week.

  • Product mastery: You’ll develop strong knowledge of our events, memberships, and education ecosystem, enabling confident and relevant cross-selling.

  • Collaboration & feedback: You’ll work closely with marketing, product, community, and customer success teams, sharing insights and operating with autonomy while knowing when to ask for support.

This Role Is For You If

  • You’re early in your career and hungry to learn, not entitled to results

  • You’re comfortable being uncomfortable while learning something new

  • You actively seek feedback and apply it quickly

  • You take ownership for outcomes, not just effort

  • You’re resilient, organised, and able to manage pace and pressure

  • You communicate clearly with customers and with teammates

  • You enjoy working as part of a team where success is shared

Our Hiring Process

Our hiring process is designed to reflect how we actually work: collaborative, practical, and focused on potential rather than polish.

  • First interview (values, motivation, and learning mindset)

  • One-day assessment in our London office (practical exercises, collaboration, and real-world sales scenarios)

  • Final shortlist: up to 3 candidates selected into an onboarding cohort, starting together and learning side-by-side

This process helps us understand how you think, learn, and show up — not just how well you interview.

Compensation: Base Salary £26,500 - 28,000 *range depending on experience

Commissions:
Year 1 OTE £35,000 uncapped
Year 2 OTE £55,000 uncapped

_________________________________

Benefits

Time off & flexibility

  • 34 days’ paid holiday including UK Bank holidays and a day off on your birthday

  • Flexible working hours: our core hours are 10am–4:30pm, with the flexibility to structure your working day between 8am and 8pm around when you work best

  • Work from where works for you: choose to work remotely within the UK or hybrid from our London office. Our office is always open to the wider team whenever you fancy coming in

  • WFH Kit: a comprehensive tech setup, plus a dedicated WFH equipment budget

  • A well-stocked office: snacks, drinks and fresh fruit available in our London office

Health & wellbeing

  • Private Medical and Dental Insurance with Bupa

  • Life Insurance: cover worth 4x your annual salary

  • On-demand therapy & coaching: company sponsored access to therapy and career coaching through Spill

  • Wellness perks: discounts on gym memberships, fitness and wellness classes

  • Cycle to Work & Workplace Nursery schemes

  • Perks at Work: access to a wide range of corporate discounts

  • Monthly flexible benefits allowance through ThanksBen (£50/month in year one, £100/month in year two and £165/month from year three), giving you extra flexibility to spend on the benefits that matter most to you

Learning & development

  • A growing personal L&D budget (starting at £500 per year and increasing with tenure to £3,000 per year)

  • Dedicated L&D or volunteering time: one paid day every quarter to invest in your development or support a cause you care about.

  • Unlimited access to our internal Academy: including courses, learning resources and professional certifications

Community and Inclusion

We are committed to creating a workplace that is free from discrimination and bias, and where everyone has equal opportunities to succeed and contribute. We acknowledge that our work here is never done - and we promise to continue striving for inclusivity every day.

If you’re worried you don’t quite hit all the requirements we’ve listed, don’t let that hold you back from submitting your application! Unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are essential for our ability to innovate and grow, so if you think you’d be a great fit then we’d love to hear from you.

We are The Alliance - in more ways than one.

Compensation: £26.5K – £28K • £10K – £20K Commission

We connect industry leaders and innovators through unparalleled networking opportunities. We bring together leading minds to share the latest trends, challenges and opportunities facing companies, the tactics and tools needed to drive results, and a forum to make meaningful connections.

Our Alliance brand is renowned for its VIP dinners, exclusive breakfasts, and bespoke 1-2-1 meeting packages designed to bridge supply and demand across various verticals. Join our dynamic team and drive sales to new commercial prospects, creating valuable connections and driving business growth.

The Role

We’re looking for a commercially driven VIP Event Sponsorship Sales Executive to take ownership of our high-level, invitation-only dinner series and related bespoke experiences.

You’ll focus on selling sponsorship packages to top-tier B2B brands looking to engage with senior audiences through intimate, content-driven environments. These conversations often serve as the entry point to broader partnership discussions, including full-series or multi-event sponsorships, making this a role with both immediate and strategic impact.

You’ll work closely with our wider event sponsorship team to identify opportunities, open doors, and nurture long-term commercial relationships that span across our community portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

  • Executive Event Sales: Lead sponsorship sales for The Alliance’s portfolio of exclusive, invite-only dinners and professional experiences.

  • New Business Development: Proactively identify, target, and secure sponsorship opportunities with prospective clients across both existing Alliance communities and new markets.

  • Client Outreach & Relationship Building: Re-engage existing clients from our digital and event portfolios, cultivating long-term sponsorship partnerships.

  • Revenue Growth: Consistently deliver new business revenue through proactive outreach, pitching, and closing bespoke event sponsorship deals.

  • Consultative Sales Approach: Understand client objectives and position bespoke event solutions that deliver tangible ROI.

  • Market Insight & Opportunity Creation: Stay ahead of B2B event trends to spot new opportunities, feeding insights back to product and event teams.

  • Pipeline Management: Maintain disciplined pipeline management, accurate forecasting, and consistent progress toward monthly and quarterly targets.

  • Collaboration: Work cross-functionally with events, marketing, content, and community teams to ensure flawless delivery of sponsorship packages.

  • Reporting & Feedback: Provide regular sales performance updates, client feedback, and market insights to inform ongoing strategy.

Requirements
If the below sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you:

  • Proven track record in event or sponsorship sales, ideally within B2B, media, or conferences.

  • You have a deep understanding of prospecting and developing strong relationships with enterprise customers

  • You’ll be determined and focused, and enjoy the challenge of hunting and closing net new business

  • Tough targets won’t scare you and you’ll have a demonstrable track record of not just meeting them - but exceeding them

  • Confidence to experiment with different tactics, shake up strategy, adapt to new trends, to incorporate new products, changes, or to bounce back from subpar results

  • You want ownership in your role from the beginning and ready to level up.

  • You expertly balance and prioritise your daily to-do's, as well as your short-term and long-term planning

  • Experience with Asana or project management tools a plus (desirable)

Location: This role can be either Hybrid in our London office or completely remote across the UK (not abroad).

Salary: Base Salary range £32K - £38K (*Based on previous experience) - OTE £70K+

_______________________

Benefits

Time off & flexibility

  • 34 days’ paid holiday including UK Bank holidays and a day off on your birthday

  • Flexible working hours: our core hours are 10am–4:30pm, with the flexibility to structure your working day between 8am and 8pm around when you work best

  • Work from where works for you: choose to work remotely within the UK or hybrid from our London office. Our office is always open to the wider team whenever you fancy coming in

  • WFH Kit: a comprehensive tech setup, plus a dedicated WFH equipment budget

Health & wellbeing

Lead Product Designer - Cortex

📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH)

💰 Competitive salary, dependent on experience

 

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to transform the experience of buying, selling, renting and letting property, elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.

 

Cortex is an exciting new product that brings agentic AI into Street and Spectre, taking on the busywork so agents can focus on winning instructions and building relationships. It's early, moving fast, and will ultimately touch every part of the product suite. We're looking for a Lead Product Designer to shape what agentic UX looks like across all of it.

 

We want someone who is genuinely excited by agentic AI, past needing to be told what's worth working on, and ready to help define a product category that doesn't have a playbook yet - working closely with senior stakeholders across the business.

 

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. You'll drive direction alongside product and engineering, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

 

Here's what you can expect to be working on

  • Shape the UX of agentic AI across Street and Spectre - deciding which agency workflows agents should own, then designing how that actually feels and builds trust for the user.

  • Design across the whole suite, not one domain - valuation, prospecting, marketing, enquiry handling, sales progression, property management. You'll hold a huge amount of context.

  • Define the patterns for a new category. There's no established playbook for agentic UX in property - you'll set it.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like.

  • Prototype, test and ship at pace - getting working prototypes in front of real agents and iterating fast.

 

You should apply if:

  • You've built or shaped agentic AI, not just used AI tools - multi-step, tool-using agents you've designed, prototyped or shipped. You understand how they work and where they break.

  • You've got a well-formed point of view on agentic UX - how you design for systems that don't always behave the same way, how you build in trust, transparency and control, and when to keep a human in the loop.

  • You stay current. This field moves monthly and you keep on top of it.

  • You're energised by an undefined problem space and bring the case for what's worth doing, rather than waiting for a brief.

  • You're commercially fluent - you make design trade-offs informed by how the product performs, not just user preference. You define success before you ship and read the result after.

 

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • Your AI experience is limited to speeding up your own workflow. This role is about designing AI into the product, and that gap will show quickly.

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role - it expects materially more scope, autonomy and judgment.

  • You need a well-defined problem before you can start. Cortex is still taking shape, and that won't change soon.

  • You expect to be handed a roadmap. Here, you help write it.

 

A bit about you

  • AI & agentic depth: Non-negotiable, and the first thing we'll screen for. Current, hands-on knowledge of agentic AI, with real examples of what you've built or shaped.

  • Craft: Lead-level UX and product design. Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach.

  • Breadth: Comfortable operating across the whole product suite and holding a lot of context at once, not going deep on a single domain.

  • Ambiguity: You do your best work when the problem isn't yet defined.

  • Cross-functional: A peer at the table with product and engineering, partnering closely with a good PM without treading on each other's toes.

  • Technical fluency: Being hands-on enough to prototype with code is a real advantage here, given how close design sits to how these systems work. It's a plus, not a hard requirement.

  • Experience: Typically this comes with around 8+ years in product/UX design at senior IC level - but we care more about evidence you can operate at Lead altitude than the exact number, especially given how new agentic AI is. SaaS or complex product experience is helpful; property experience isn't required.

 

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

 

Why join Street Group?

🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week

🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!)

💪 Joining a culture that supports your development and encourages growth

📚 £500 yearly L&D budget for your career development

🎂 Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away

🙋 'Give something back' - 2 paid days volunteering on us

👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay

🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured

🧘 Regular well-being initiatives

🕒 Flexible working hours

🚂 Public transport season ticket loans

🌷 Paid menopause leave

🌞 Holiday buying scheme

🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition

👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day

👩🏿‍💻 A chance to work on cutting-edge technology

🐶 Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome!

🍻 Fully stocked fridge and beers (or an alternative) on us every Friday afternoon

🎊 Company and team off-sites, events and happy hours

🚴 Cycle to work scheme

🚗 Electric car salary sacrifice scheme

🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company!

 

Salary

We're not publishing a fixed band for this one. We'll build the package around your experience and the scope you bring, so please apply and let's have the conversation.

We care deeply about helping the tech industry become a more inclusive and diverse place and we work hard to lead by example. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a complementary team of employees and building an inclusive environment for all. Candidates must be eligible to live and work in the UK and be able to perform the work specified.

 

Interview Process

3 stages = An introductory call with one of our Talent team > Technical Interview inc. a Design & AI Task with our Head of UX > Final interview with our Co-Founder.

 

We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know.

 

A note on using AI in your job application

As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. However, our goal is to get to know and hire the authentic you - your skills, experience, and values. We don't want to hire an AI-generated version of you. We consider AI to be a valuable tool, not something that should overshadow you as an individual.

Compensation: £70K – £90K

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we're hiring

  • We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled operators like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.

  • We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

  • Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we’ll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

  • The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

  • We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

  • The operational machine behind Odin is still held together in many places by people and spreadsheets. Your job is to come in, understand every process and system, simplify, streamline and automate the shit out of it.

  • You’ll be part of a small elite team embedded in operations and working closely with existing team members to build agents that automate work.

  • We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

What you'll own

  • Understand the work, then rebuild it: You’ll get close to how our operational teams actually work - the processes, edge cases, manual steps and things that slow them down. Your job is to understand them well enough to redesign, automate and build better ways of doing them.

  • Build and automate: You’ll turn manual workflows into tools, automations and systems that make the business faster and more scalable. You’ll work autonomously and move quickly - often vibe coding something useful yourself before it ever needs traditional product or engineering resource.

  • Bridge operations and engineering: You’ll know when something can be solved with process, automation or a lightweight build, and when it genuinely needs deeper engineering work. When it does, you’ll bring Product, Design and Engineering in with the problem already understood, simplified and proven.

  • Delete things and say no: You’ll constantly question why a process exists, whether a request should be supported, and whether something is worth scaling. If a workflow exists for no good reason, you kill it. If a request creates complexity without enough value, we don’t do it.

What we're looking for

  • AI-pilled builder: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built concrete solutions to problems with no budget and no engineers. No-code tooling, scripts, spreadsheets, vibe-coded apps and more.

  • Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You’ll be working on automating a lot of numerical matters - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

  • In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

  • First principles thinker: Although you're in the details and on top of execution, you also zoom out. You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal?
    A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

  • Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. SQL, serious Excel and other experience piping data between systems are all worth having too. However, we care much more about the traits you have and things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV. If you're a few years into your career and you've already automated the shit out of your last job or built something incredible with AI, we want to talk to you.

  • You want to operate, not manage: Odin is not a place for middle management. We all get shit done, regardless of title or seniority

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up: Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed: We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership: Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty: If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service: Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

This role is probably not for you if

  • You'd rather build product than operate. Product instinct is required in this role, but a product management career is not what this is;

  • You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

  • You are risk-averse;

  • You want a 9-5;

  • You take yourself too seriously;

  • You care about working for a company that’s raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

Salary

£70k - £90k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

Hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one.

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

  • Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

About Unity Advisory

Unity Advisory is a pure-play, experience-led CFO advisory firm providing integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support. We are free from audit conflicts and AI-enabled by design, combining deep technical expertise with automation, analytics and AI built into the delivery of every engagement. We are building an alternative to traditional advisory firms, focused on clarity over complexity, outcomes over hours, and practical advice delivered at pace for CFOs making high-consequence decisions.

The Role

As a Finance Transformation Manager, you will lead workstreams within high-impact transformation programmes — working directly with CFOs and their leadership teams to re-imagine and digitise finance functions through digital technologies, streamlined processes and modern operating models.

This is a client-facing role at a firm that does things differently. There are no legacy layers here — you’ll take real ownership, shape the work, and have direct visibility of the impact you create from day one. If you’ve built strong credentials in finance transformation and want to apply them somewhere that moves at pace and actually values your expertise, this is that role.

Responsibilities

• Advise CFOs and their leadership teams on transformation priorities and approach.

• Lead and manage finance transformation workstreams across process, data and technology.

• Design future-state finance operating models tailored to client context.

• Redesign core finance processes including R2R, P2P, O2C and FP&A.

• Implement cloud-based ERP and EPM platforms, automation tools, data platforms and analytics solutions.

• Translate business requirements into practical ERP/EPM solutions and integrate technology into clients’ ecosystems.

• Drive adoption of transformation initiatives so the changes stick after we leave.

• Run executive workshops and lead steering committee updates.

• Ensure delivery on time, on budget and within scope.

• Lead, coach and develop team members.

• Contribute to go-to-market activities, proposal writing and pitch presentations.

• Support thought leadership on EPM trends and tools.

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years of experience in finance transformation including 2+ years in a consulting or advisory environment.

  • Track record of delivering high-impact tech-enabled Finance Transformation programmes.

  • Experience implementing ERP, EPM, analytics tools and automation platforms.

  • Experience in process re-engineering and operating model design.

  • Finance/Accounting qualification including ACA/ACCA/CIMA/CPA

  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills. 

Work Environment

A truly hybrid and flexible working environment. We offer the opportunity to be at the forefront of AI-driven advisory services. You’ll be working on cutting-edge projects and encouraged to deploy the latest analytical tools and approaches.

At Unity Advisory, we are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. In line with the Equality Act 2010, we will accommodate any suitable candidate requiring assistance to attend or conduct an interview. If you need any adjustments or support, please let us know when either scheduling your interview or in your application cover letter. We are dedicated to ensuring that everyone has an equal opportunity to succeed and are here to support you throughout the process.

PLEASE NOTE THAT WE DO NOT ACCEPT ANY THIRD PARTY UNSOLICITED CVS

About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Associate Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

What we're looking for

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

  • You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

  • You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

  • You're comfortable with data: you can write SQL or Python and answer your own questions

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Lendable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

  • Top-tier private health insurance

  • Offsites for the US Cards product and engineering team, and an annual whole-company trip abroad (previously Turkey and France)

Interview process

We respect your time and move quickly:

  1. Intro call (remote) - 30 minutes with the hiring manager

  2. Take-home exercise (remote) - a practical product challenge in your own time, followed by a video debrief with two members of the product team

  3. Final round (in our London office) - typically with the CPO and US Cards MD, Engineering Manager, Head of Product and hiring manager

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.

Check out our blog!

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

What we're looking for

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

  • You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

  • You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

  • You're comfortable with data: you can write SQL or Python and answer your own questions

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Lendable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

  • Top-tier private health insurance

  • Offsites for the US Cards product and engineering team, and an annual whole-company trip abroad (previously Turkey and France)

Interview process

We respect your time and move quickly:

  1. Intro call (remote) - 30 minutes with the hiring manager

  2. Take-home exercise (remote) - a practical product challenge in your own time, followed by a video debrief with two members of the product team

  3. Final round (in our London office) - typically with the CPO and US Cards MD, Engineering Manager, Head of Product and hiring manager

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations
